# Briefly

> Briefly is an AI knowledge base for financial advisors and wealth firms, built to run inside Claude. It connects a firm's own documents, email, meeting notes, and portfolio data into one place, and every answer cites back to the source it came from.

Briefly runs two ways. The Claude connector is the flagship path. It's a download that adds Briefly to Claude Desktop and reads from a folder on your own computer. With the Briefly connector, client files never reach Briefly's servers. Only your sign-in, a seat check, de-identified preference rules, and a short usage record for each tool call do, and Claude reads the files under your firm's own Claude plan. The web app is the second surface, a browser workspace for firms that would rather sign in than install anything, and its files live in Briefly's hosted environment instead.

Briefly is built by Briefly Wealth LLC, founded by Connor Florczyk.

These files are intended to help LLMs and AI agents accurately ground answers about Briefly in primary source pages rather than third-party summaries. For a flat plain-text concatenation of the main marketing pages, see `/llms-full.txt`.

## Product

- [Home](https://www.brieflywealth.com/): Briefly is an AI knowledge base for financial advisors that runs inside Claude. Ask across your firm's own files and get cited answers. With the connector, client files never reach our servers.
- [Knowledge base](https://www.brieflywealth.com/knowledge-base): How Briefly builds an AI knowledge base for financial advisors from a firm's own documents, email, meeting notes, and portfolio data, with every fact traceable to its source.
- [Compare](https://www.brieflywealth.com/compare): The Briefly connector and the web app side by side. Both read from the same client file, cited and correctable. With the connector, client files stay on the advisor's computer.
- [Download](https://www.brieflywealth.com/download): Download the Briefly connector for Claude Desktop. Client files stay on your computer, and only sign-in and de-identified rules reach Briefly's server.
- [Start](https://www.brieflywealth.com/start): Sign up for the Briefly connector without a call. Checkout runs on Stripe.

## Guides

- [Claude for financial advisors](https://www.brieflywealth.com/claude-for-financial-advisors): What Claude can do for financial advisors out of the box, why it can't see your client files by default, and four ways to change that, with a plain data-access comparison against ChatGPT.
- [ChatGPT and Claude compliance for financial advisors](https://www.brieflywealth.com/ai-compliance-for-financial-advisors): What Reg S-P, the SEC, and FINRA require before an advisor puts client data into ChatGPT or Claude, and what advisors use instead.

## Company

- [Security](https://www.brieflywealth.com/security): With the Briefly connector, client files stay on the advisor's computer. Covers exactly what reaches Briefly's servers, how Reg S-P applies, and answers for compliance officers.
- [About](https://www.brieflywealth.com/about): Briefly Wealth LLC, founded by Connor Florczyk. With the connector, client files never reach Briefly's servers. Why he built Briefly and what the product principles are.

## Examples

- [Sample deliverables](https://www.brieflywealth.com/sample-deliverables): Five real Briefly deliverables, a quarterly review, a goal analysis, a month-end letter, a deal summary, and a correction-loop example, with names and firms fictionalized.
- [Sample quarterly review](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-quarterly-review): Performance for the quarter, allocation drift against policy, and the conversations worth having next, cited back to the source files.
- [Sample goal analysis](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-goal-analysis): Each goal priced against a household's actual accounts, with funding gaps named and every figure traceable to a statement.
- [Sample month-end commentary](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-month-end-commentary): A month-end letter showing household totals, what moved since last month, and the market backdrop, written for the client and cited for the advisor.
- [Sample deal summary](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-deal-summary): Terms, traction, and the three biggest risks of a private deal, condensed into a one-page brief a committee can act on.
- [Sample correction loop](https://www.brieflywealth.com/samples/sample-correction-loop): How one detail from a meeting note becomes a standing rule Briefly applies to every brief after. Names and firms are fictionalized.
- [Sample Morning Brief](https://www.brieflywealth.com/sample-brief): A sample edition of Briefly's Morning Brief email, with a pre-market table, an advisor talking point, and what to watch that week. Illustrative, not real client data.

## Blog

- [Blog](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog): Writing on advisor workflows, portfolio prep, and client communication from the Briefly team.
- [The Jobs AI Won't Replace](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/jobs-ai-wont-replace): Advisors, lawyers, and doctors stay hard to replace because the value in the work is trust, judgment, and accountability, not information processing. Published December 17, 2025.
- [Your Brain Doesn't Have Enough RAM](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/your-brain-doesnt-have-enough-ram): Advisors hit a real memory limit managing 100-plus households, and the fix is surfacing the right context at the right time instead of trying to remember everything. Published January 3, 2026.
- [The Great Wealth Transfer Trap](https://www.brieflywealth.com/blog/great-wealth-transfer-trap): As wealth splits across heirs, an advisor's assets under management can stay flat while the number of relationships to manage multiplies, straining the economics of the book. Published November 5, 2025.

## Newsletter

- [Morning Brief subscribe](https://www.brieflywealth.com/subscribe): A daily weekday email covering what moved overnight, what's on the calendar, and a talking point advisors can use with clients that day. Free for financial advisors.
